kicker: Vivix W1, a streaming video model

scenes.headline: How a video model streams while you steer it
scenes.sub: Vivix W1: chunked video and audio, generated as you watch
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Strobe! Vivix sells W1 as real-time interactive video. Here's how a model like that streams.

scenes.text: Generate the video in short chunks, each one conditioned on the chunks already made and on whatever the user just did.
scenes.mark: on whatever the user just did
scenes.say: The idea: make video in short chunks, each one looking back at the last, and at what the user just did.

scenes.title: Two ways to make a clip

left.title: Clip at once
items: Every frame sees every other frame
Nothing is done until all of it is
No way to change course midway
left.say: A clip model denoises every frame together. Nothing is done until all of it is.

right.title: Chunk by chunk
items: Each chunk sees only the past
Playback starts on the first chunk
New input shapes the next chunk
right.say: A streaming model goes in order, so new input shapes the next chunk.

steps.say: References anchor the world once, at the start.
The user's latest input goes in at every step.
A diffusion transformer denoises the next chunk, picture and sound together.
That chunk joins the cache, and the next step reads it.

steps.note: diffusion runs one chunk ahead of the decoder
steps.say: On the server, diffusion runs one chunk ahead of the decoder.
An interrupt preempts the chunk in flight, in about six hundred milliseconds on average, by Vivix's count.

scenes.title: Two problems every streaming model has

items.say: Fifty sampling steps can't keep up, so the model is distilled to a few.
And each chunk inherits the last one's mistakes, so long streams drift.
Vivix benchmarks its fix only on small models and short clips.

scenes.title: An hour of generated video, US dollars
scenes.note: async clips at 720p; the streaming W1 has no price yet
scenes.say: An hour of W1 output costs about eleven dollars at its cheapest tier, against hundreds for clip models. But that's the job queue, not the stream.

scenes.label: real-time factor: generation time divided by clip length
scenes.note: 8.4 s to make an 8 s clip, Vivix's own timing
scenes.say: Eight point four seconds to make eight seconds of video. Right at real time.

scenes.text: Streaming comes from chunked, causal generation; the clip queue is cheap today, and the steerable stream is still a private beta.
scenes.say: The clip queue is cheap today. The stream you can steer is still in private beta.

recap: Chunks, each conditioned on the past
Diffusion one chunk ahead of the decoder
Cheap clips now, the stream in beta
scenes.say: Chunks that look back, a pipeline one step ahead, and a stream you can't rent yet.
